# Crossio: Custom Crosshair — Product and Policy Reference

Crossio displays a user-selected crosshair as a customizable Android visual layer. Users can select built-in designs, adjust color, size, thickness, gap, outline and opacity, import a transparent PNG locally, save designs, and control the overlay.

## Overlay architecture

The main crosshair uses Android's `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` capability and a foreground service. It is configured as click-through and cannot receive touch or key input. A separate optional mini control overlay is touchable because it provides user controls for visibility and position. Users can enable optional auto-start inside the app; when enabled, Crossio may restart the selected overlay when the app opens. The active service can be stopped from its persistent notification.

Crossio does not read or modify another app's code, memory, files, data, or network traffic. It does not capture another app's screen and provides no auto-aim, auto-tap, macro, input injection, accessibility-based input generation, or game automation.

## Permissions

- `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`: displays the crosshair and optional controls above other apps.
- Foreground service and notifications: keep the active layer visible to Android and provide a persistent Stop action.
- Optional battery-optimization exemption: may help on devices that aggressively stop foreground services.
- Image selection: lets the user choose a custom image; modern Android's system picker is used without legacy broad storage permissions.

## Data processing

The app uses Firebase Analytics for general interaction events and diagnostic properties, Crashlytics for crash reports, Cloud Messaging for notification tokens, anonymous Firebase authentication, and Firestore for configuration and campaign metadata. Google Mobile Ads may process advertising identifiers, IP-derived approximate region, interactions, and device data. RevenueCat handles subscription status, purchase validation, and categorical engagement attributes used to select subscription offers. Google Play handles billing.

Imported crosshair images are processed in local app storage and are not uploaded to flappsio servers for this feature. Crosshair names, full crosshair definitions, and local file paths are not included in Firebase Analytics events. Device-side engagement counters may be converted into categorical attributes and sent to RevenueCat when campaign rules are configured.

## Third-party rules

Some games and competitive platforms may restrict visual overlays. The user is responsible for checking current rules. Crossio is independent and is not endorsed or approved by third-party game developers, publishers, or platforms. No claim of universal compatibility, competitive advantage, guaranteed safety, or protection from account enforcement is made.

## Web tool

The Crossio website includes a free browser-based crosshair creator. It previews a design against neutral backgrounds and exports a transparent 512×512 PNG locally in the browser.
